description: The color comes from the product recorded on the invoice line itself (Invoice_Line_Items.product_id).

a.request: Take each invoice line item and match it to its order item by `order_item_id` (line items with no matching order item are dropped). Find the product through the invoice line's own `product_id` (`Invoice_Line_Items.product_id`), not the `product_id` on the order item, dropping rows with no matching product, and use that product's color. Group by the invoice line's order item id and that product color. For each group, give the order item id, the product color, the average invoiced quantity (`Invoice_Line_Items.product_quantity`), and the average of (`derived_product_cost` − `derived_total_cost`) / `derived_total_cost`, ignoring missing values in both averages. Then, within each color, rank the groups by average quantity, highest first (missing values last; ties share a rank and the next rank is skipped), keep those ranked 3 or better, and show the rank as a fifth column. Don't round anything.
a.sql: WITH g AS (SELECT ili.order_item_id AS order_item_id, p.product_color AS product_color, AVG(CAST(ili.product_quantity AS REAL)) AS avg_quantity, AVG((ili.derived_product_cost - ili.derived_total_cost) / ili.derived_total_cost) AS avg_cost_ratio FROM Invoice_Line_Items ili JOIN Order_Items oi ON oi.order_item_id = ili.order_item_id JOIN Products p ON p.product_id = ili.product_id GROUP BY ili.order_item_id, p.product_color), r AS (SELECT order_item_id, product_color, avg_quantity, avg_cost_ratio, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY product_color ORDER BY CASE WHEN avg_quantity IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END, avg_quantity DESC) AS qty_rank FROM g) SELECT order_item_id, product_color, avg_quantity, avg_cost_ratio, qty_rank FROM r WHERE qty_rank <= 3

c.request: Match each invoice line item to its order item by `order_item_id` (dropping line items without one) and bring in the product's color (dropping rows where the product isn't found). Group by order item id and product color. For each group, give the order item id, the color, the average invoiced quantity (`product_quantity`), and the average of (`derived_product_cost` − `derived_total_cost`) / `derived_total_cost`, ignoring missing values. Then, within each color, rank the groups by average quantity from highest to lowest (missing values last; ties share a rank and the next rank is skipped) and keep ranks 1 to 3, showing the rank as a fifth column. No rounding. The color comes from the product recorded on the invoice line itself (Invoice_Line_Items.product_id).
c.sql: WITH g AS (SELECT ili.order_item_id AS order_item_id, p.product_color AS product_color, AVG(CAST(ili.product_quantity AS REAL)) AS avg_quantity, AVG((ili.derived_product_cost - ili.derived_total_cost) / ili.derived_total_cost) AS avg_cost_ratio FROM Invoice_Line_Items ili JOIN Order_Items oi ON ili.order_item_id = oi.order_item_id JOIN Products p ON ili.product_id = p.product_id WHERE ili.order_item_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY ili.order_item_id, p.product_color), r AS (SELECT order_item_id, product_color, avg_quantity, avg_cost_ratio, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY product_color ORDER BY CASE WHEN avg_quantity IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END, avg_quantity DESC) AS rnk FROM g) SELECT order_item_id, product_color, avg_quantity, avg_cost_ratio, rnk FROM r WHERE rnk <= 3

b.request: Join Invoice_Line_Items to Order_Items on order_item_id and to Products on the line item's own product_id (Invoice_Line_Items.product_id) to get product_color. Then group by order_item_id and product_color. For each group, return the average product_quantity and the average of (derived_product_cost − derived_total_cost) / derived_total_cost, ignoring NULLs. Within each color, rank the groups by average quantity descending (NULLs last, ties share a rank and the next rank is skipped) and keep ranks 1–3, with the rank as the fifth column and no rounding
b.sql: SELECT order_item_id, product_color, avg_quantity, avg_ratio, rnk FROM (SELECT ili.order_item_id AS order_item_id, p.product_color AS product_color, AVG(CAST(ili.product_quantity AS REAL)) AS avg_quantity, AVG((CAST(ili.derived_product_cost AS REAL) - ili.derived_total_cost) / ili.derived_total_cost) AS avg_ratio, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY p.product_color ORDER BY (AVG(CAST(ili.product_quantity AS REAL)) IS NULL), AVG(CAST(ili.product_quantity AS REAL)) DESC) AS rnk FROM Invoice_Line_Items ili JOIN Order_Items oi ON ili.order_item_id = oi.order_item_id JOIN Products p ON ili.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY ili.order_item_id, p.product_color) t WHERE rnk <= 3

d.request: Match each invoice line item to its order item by `order_item_id` (dropping line items without one), and bring in the product's color from the product recorded on the invoice line itself (`Invoice_Line_Items.product_id`), dropping rows where the product isn't found. Group by order item id and product color. For each group, give the order item id, the color, the average invoiced quantity (`product_quantity`), and the average of (`derived_product_cost` − `derived_total_cost`) / `derived_total_cost`, ignoring missing values. Then, within each color, rank the groups by average quantity from highest to lowest (missing values last; ties share a rank and the next rank is skipped) and keep ranks 1 to 3, showing the rank as a fifth column. No rounding.
d.sql: SELECT order_item_id, product_color, avg_qty, avg_ratio, rnk FROM (SELECT order_item_id, product_color, avg_qty, avg_ratio, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY product_color ORDER BY (avg_qty IS NULL), avg_qty DESC) AS rnk FROM (SELECT oi.order_item_id AS order_item_id, p.product_color AS product_color, AVG(CAST(ili.product_quantity AS REAL)) AS avg_qty, AVG((ili.derived_product_cost - ili.derived_total_cost) / ili.derived_total_cost) AS avg_ratio FROM Invoice_Line_Items ili JOIN Order_Items oi ON ili.order_item_id = oi.order_item_id JOIN Products p ON ili.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY oi.order_item_id, p.product_color) g) r WHERE rnk <= 3
